question: A sum of money doubled itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 10 years. In how many years will it become eight times?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__****Given**

Time = 10 years

Amount = 2 principal

**Calculation**

 A certain sum at C.I. becomes n times in t years then,

n times → t years

nm times → (m × t) years

A sum of money placed at C.I. doubles itself in 10 years then,

2 times → 10 years

8 times = 2³ times = (3 × 10) years = 30 years

**∴ In 30 years , principal will become 8 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given**

Time = 10 years

Amount = 2 principal

**Formula used**

Amount = P(1 +r%)t

where P, r and t represents principal, rate and time respectively

**Calculation**

let Principal is Rs.x

Amount = 2x

Rate = r

Time = 10 years

2x = x(1 + r%)¹⁰

⇒ 2 = (1 + r%)¹⁰ ---- (1)

8x = x(1 + r%)t

⇒ 8 = (1 + r%)t

(2)³ = (1 +r%)t

⇒ [(1 + r%)¹⁰]³ = (1 + r%)t (from 1)

⇒ (1 +r%)³⁰ = (1 + r%)t

⇒ 30 = t

**∴ In 30 years , principal will become 8 times.**
